book_understanding.teaching_order: A textbook would define small finance banks and payments banks with their eligibility, capital and permitted activities. The video starts with the gap (a 140-crore crowd of which banks reach only a shaded part), states the national goal, lists RBI's reasons why ordinary banks cannot close the gap, and only then introduces differentiated banks as the answer. Small banks are taught as three features each answering a reason (target the poor in a fixed area, cut cost with technology, also serve city slums). Payments banks are taught as a story (wallet apps already reached the unbanked, so RBI licensed them), then their limits are explained with reasons and a loophole RBI anticipated. Examples and the naming rule come last.
book_understanding.breakdown_rule: Start from one problem picture (who is not reached), give the official reasons, then teach each new institution as features or limits that answer those reasons, each limit with its 'why'.

narration.density: About 24 terms (financial inclusion, cooperative bank, regional rural bank, MFI sector, operating cost, transaction cost, unbanked, underserved, differentiated bank, small finance bank, payments bank, targeted approach, marginalised section, area of operation, technology driven, operational flexibility, digital wallet, fintech, licence, demand deposit, remittance, credit lending, credit history, default rate, NBFC, subsidiary) in about 8.6 minutes, about 3 per minute. talmel_summary: The picture carries the argument in the problem and small-bank parts: a shaded share of a 140-crore crowd for who is reached, circles in the crowd with dotted lines from small banks for targeting, a ring of tech icons for technology. Payments banks get a strong gate picture (wallets pass through an RBI licence card and come out as a bank, credit lending struck, the NBFC path blocked by an X). Most changes land together with their words; the weak parts are the 50 s of reason boxes, the real minister's photo and quote, and the pasted lists of bank names at the end.

voice.notes: About 187 words per minute, conversational. Unpacks with 'kehne ka matlab yeh ki' and 'yaani'. Quotes RBI in the second person as a strict elder ('pehle tum basic banking features ke saath logon ko jodo, credit lending ke chakkar mein mat pado') and uses 'jugaad' for the loophole, which lightens the regulatory part. Large numbers in Indian units ('140 crore'); years read in full ('2014-15'). Signposts are frequent and plain ('sabse pehle baat karte hain', 'chaliye ab samajhte hain'). Ends without a recap.

game_ideas.player_does: With a limited budget, places bank types over the 140-crore crowd: a costly commercial branch, a cheap small bank locked to one licensed district, or a payments bank reaching people through phones.
game_ideas.process_happens: The yellow 'reached' shade grows over the crowd where each bank serves; clusters of farmers, small shops and city-slum households light up when reached.
game_ideas.win: Shade at least the target share, including the marginalised clusters and an urban slum cluster, within budget.
game_ideas.lose: Spending everything on commercial branches reaches few people; placing a small bank outside its licensed district gets an RBI 'not allowed' stamp.
game_ideas.concept: financial inclusion and the roles of small and payments banks

game_ideas.player_does: Drags service cards (accept deposits, payments, remittance, internet banking, give loans, open an NBFC) into the licence of a small bank or a payments bank.
game_ideas.process_happens: Allowed services settle into the bank's list; 'give loans' dropped on the payments bank is struck in red with the credit-risk reason, and 'open an NBFC' draws a dotted arrow that hits a red X.
game_ideas.lose: A wrong placement plays the struck line or the blocked arrow and asks why (no credit history, high defaults).
game_ideas.concept: what a payments bank may and may not do

game_ideas.player_does: Plays a wallet company growing from bill payments to a payments bank: applies to RBI, picks a name, picks services, and tries a shortcut to lending.
game_ideas.process_happens: The wallet icon passes the RBI licence card if criteria are met; a name without 'Payments Bank' is sent back; the lending shortcut through an NBFC is blocked.
game_ideas.win: Becomes a licensed payments bank serving people who never had an account.
game_ideas.lose: Trying to lend or to skip the name rule shows RBI's reason and resets that step.
game_ideas.concept: how and why payments banks were created and limited

game_ideas.player_does: Links each reason traditional banks fail (high running cost, high fees, unsuitable products) to the small-bank feature that answers it (tech-driven, targeted, flexible).
game_ideas.process_happens: Each correct link draws a line from the pink reason box to the lit sidebar feature and shades a little more of the crowd.
game_ideas.win: All three reasons answered and the crowd shade grows.
game_ideas.lose: A wrong link shows the reason box staying pink and the crowd unchanged.
game_ideas.concept: why differentiated banks were designed this way

checks_learned: Counts said must match lists shown (10 small banks said; the table shows more rows).
Dates on screen must match the narration (wallets 'from 2006' in voice, 'before 2013' on screen).
No real person photos or quotes as decoration; cite the source in text only.
Every 'not allowed' rule should be shown as a struck item or a blocked arrow (E34 does both; enforce it).
A reasons list held as text for more than about 40 s should be flagged; each reason needs its own small picture.
Elements with no stated meaning (the row of thin up-arrows) should be flagged as decoration.
Superlative claims ('first in the world') must be marked for fact-checking before reuse.
Reusing the opening problem picture for a later idea (the crowd box for wallets) should be encouraged, so the learner compares slices.

teaching_best.why: A shaded part of a 140-crore crowd dropping down to the banks that reach it makes 'who is banked' visible with almost no words.
Small banks drop dotted lines into circled clusters of the crowd: targeting and a limited area in one picture.
The Mumbai neighbourhood example explains why a 'rural' bank type is allowed in cities.
The wallet story gives the reason payments banks exist before naming their rules, and the licence card works as a gate.
Each limit has its reason (no credit history, high defaults) and the anticipated loophole (NBFC subsidiary) is shown as a blocked path.
Corrects a likely wrong inference (you must be a wallet first) right after the story that could cause it.

teaching_weak.why: The three reasons are pink text boxes for about 50 s with no picture.
A real minister's photo and a long quote decorate the priority claim.
Differentiated banks are defined by one sentence in a box; the idea of a narrower licence is not pictured.
Pasted lists of real bank names; the spoken counts do not match the rows.
'Cost-effective because of technology' is only said; the ring of icons does not show any cost falling.
